As part of the procurement process, the OGP is issuing this Preliminary Market Consultation (PMC) document and invites responses from Economic Operators in the stenography and transcription services market. This is a market sounding exercise to obtain market information on the provision of stenography and transcription services to assist in the development and structuring of the upcoming Request for Tenders. This is also an opportunity for market players to provide valuable information to the OGP in respect of any issues or challenges relevant to this market and to submit any suggestions which would enhance the provision of stenography and transcription services for Public Sector Bodies (PSBs) in Ireland. It is not a call for competition. Details of the procurement process pursuant to this

To ascertain the specific measures undertaken by the market to align with Ireland’s Climate Action Plan 2025 to become carbon neutral by no later than 2050 (Climate Action Plan 2025). Background to the Procurement Requirements The OGP is considering the establishment of the most appropriate, responsive, and effective procurement solution for the provision of professional stenography and transcription services to Public Service Bodies. The framework will support the accurate, secure, and timely capture of spoken communications across a wide range of official settings, with services provided by Economic Operators using their skills, experience, expertise, and professionalism to deliver value-added solutions. Services may include stenographic and court reporting, transcription, captioning, inquiry reporting, remote and hybrid hearing support, and secure transcript management for interviews, hearings, inquiries, tribunals, public consultations, committee meetings, disciplinary proceedings, investigations, conferences, workshops, stakeholder engagements, and other official proceedings. Stenography is the process of creating an accurate, verbatim record of spoken words using specialist shorthand techniques and stenotype technology. Qualified stenographers attend proceedings in person or remotely and use computerised stenographic equipment to capture speech in real time. This enables the production of highly accurate transcripts, often available immediately upon completion of a hearing or proceeding. Depending on the requirements of the Framework Client, stenographers may also create audio recordings and maintain contemporaneous notes to support transcript verification and quality assurance processes. Transcription services involve the conversion of recorded audio and video content into written records. These services may be provided using traditional human transcription methods, AI-assisted transcription technologies, or a combination of both. Transcripts may be produced in verbatim, edited verbatim, or intelligent transcription formats, depending on the purpose and requirements of the assignment. L’accord- cadre est un contrat, conclu entre l’acheteur et un opérateur économique public ou privé, ayant pour objet d’établir les termes régissant les marchés ou les bons de commandes à passer au cours d’une période donnée. A chaque besoin, l’acheteur émettra soit un bon de commande sur la base du bordereau de prix unitaires joint au présent accord-cadre soit rédigera un marché subséquent. Dans ce dernier cas, un dossier de consultation (comprenant un acte d’engagement, un cahier des clauses particulières et une lettre de consultation) sera adressé au titulaire de l’accord-cadre précisant les caractéristiques et les modalités d’exécution des prestations demandées. Le titulaire remettra alors une proposition tech

suivantes : 1. Le présent accord cadre est passé en application de l’article L124-4 du Code de la Sécurité sociale, de l’arrêté du 19 juillet 2018 relatif aux marchés des organismes de sécurité sociale et des dispositions du Code de la Commande publique. L’accord-cadre est régi par référence aux Cahiers des Clauses Administratives Générales et Techniques applicables aux Marchés Publics de Fournitures Courantes et de Services (C.C.A.G.F.C.S.) (Arrêté du 30 mars 2021 paru au Journal Officiel du 1er avril 2021). 3.2 : CONDITIONS JURIDIQUES DE L’ACCORD-CADRE Il s’agit d’un accord-cadre exécuté au moyen de bons de commandes, conclu avec un seul opérateur économique, sans minimum et avec un maximum de 250 000 € HT. L’accord cadre sur la durée de vingt-quatre (24) mois est estimé à environ 14 000 plis. N4571A-27-R-0002 Page 13 of 106 Truth-seeking means the LLM is truthful in responding to user prompts seeking factual information or analysis. The LLM prioritizes historical accuracy, scientific inquiry, and objectivity, and acknowledges uncertainty where reliable information is incomplete or contradictory. Ideological Neutrality means the LLM is a neutral, nonpartisan tool that does not manipulate responses in favor of ideological dogmas. Significant Modifications means any changes made by the contractor or subcontractor to the AI model that could reasonably be expected to alter its adherence to the Unbiased AI Principles. For the purposes of compliance with the Unbiased AI Principles, this definition includes, but is not limited to, changes to training data and model architecture, and alterations to filtering and content moderation. (b) Contractor Obligation. The contractor must ensure that any LLM or other AI model provided under this contract complies with the Unbiased AI Principles throughout the period of performance. Its use also creates important responsibilities for public bodies and their staff in relation to responsible use, data protection, information security, transparency, accountability and human oversight. The purpose of the training is to establish a consistent baseline level of AI literacy across the sector and provide staff with the knowledge required to understand AI, recognise the responsibilities associated with its use, and use AI appropriately and responsibly within a public-service environment. The training suite will cover seven topics: AI fundamentals; Responsible AI; Public service obligations; Data protection considerations; Information security considerations; Human oversight; and Awareness of the EU AI Act. The training is intended as baseline awareness training for staff generally and is not intended to provide specialist, technical or role-specific AI training. This reflects the current sector approach of providing a universal AI literacy baseline separately from practical tool-specific enablement. The successful tenderer will work with the LGMA and its nominated representatives to agree the structure, learning objectives and detailed content of each module before development commences. All content will be subject to review and final approval

entity_geography.text: e Articulate Storyline is used, or the equivalent editable source file or course where another agreed authoring tool is used. Provide post-delivery technical and module support should issues or bugs arise. Undertake a minimum of one independent external accessibility audit per annum of digital learning solutions developed under the contract, addressing compliance with WCAG 2.2, EN 301 549 and agreed accessibility requirements. Audit findings and remediation actions shall be provided to ESB. ESB will retain full ownership of all customised and developed learning content. ESB requires that Personal Data be hosted in the European Economic Area (EEA) or where appropriate in another EU approved country. For each individual call-off/drawdown contract, a separate Project Agreement incorporating the terms and conditions of the framework agreement shall be signed by the parties to the contract. ESB was established in 1927 as a statutory corporation in the Republic of Ireland under the Electricity (Supply) Act 1927. With a holding of approximately 97.1%, ESB is majority owned by the Irish Government. The remaining approximate 2.9% is held by the trustees of an Employee Share Ownership Plan. As a strong, diversified, vertically integrated utility, ESB operates right across the electricity market: from generation, through transmission and distribution, to supply. In addition, ESB extracts further value at certain points along this chain: supplying gas, using our networks to carry fibre for telecommunications, developing electric vehicle public charging infrastructure and more. ESB is a leading Irish utility focused on providing excellent customer service and maintaining our financial strength. We have a regulated asset base of approximately €12 billion with 30% of electricity generation capacity in the all-island market.

Situering van De Werkvennootschap en situering van de Opdracht De Werkvennootschap werkt o.a. samen met het departement Mobiliteit en Openbare Werken en het Agentschap Wegen en Verkeer om een aantal strategisch belangrijke mobiliteitsprojecten in Vlaanderen te realiseren. Via-Invest werd hiertoe op 9 mei 2017 omgevormd in een naamloze vennootschap van publiek recht, genoemd “De Werkvennootschap”, die als projecteigenaar meer slagkracht zal hebben. De Werkvennootschap heeft als enige aandeelhouder het Vlaamse Gewest. De Werkvennootschap heeft als opdracht complexe mobiliteitsinfrastructuur van strategisch belang te realiseren en te faciliteren voor het Vlaamse Gewest en publiekrechtelijke rechtspersonen. De Werkvennootschap wenst voor de ontwikkeling van systemen inzake geïntegreerde procesbeheersing in het kader van haar projecten beroep te doen op een dienstverlener via onderhavige Opdracht. Ein Lieferant möchte auf die Mittel einer anderen Wirtschaftseinheit zurückgreifen (wie im Königlichen Erlass vom 18. Juni 2017, Artikel 72§1, vorgesehen). Ein Lieferant kann einen Qualifizierungsantrag stellen und für die Qualifizierungskriterien, die Anforderungen in Bezug auf die wirtschaftliche, finanzielle oder technische Leistungsfähigkeit sowie berufliche Befähigung enthalten (3.3.2 und 3.3.3), die Kapazitäten anderer Wirtschaftseinheiten in Anspruch nehmen. Mit anderer Wirtschaftseinheit ist eine andere (natürliche oder juristische) Person als der Lieferant selbst gemeint. Möchte ein Lieferant die Mittel einer anderen Wirtschaftseinheit in Anspruch nehmen, so gibt er dies in der Frage in Teil II C der EEE an. Möchte ein Lieferant die Mittel einer anderen Wirtschaftseinheit in Anspruch nehmen, so muss er zusätzlich zu einer EEE diese Wirtschaftseinheit veranlassen, den Abschnitt „Leistungsfähigkeit Dritter“ in Anhang 3 auszufüllen. Ohne diese Anlage kann der Lieferant eine solche Leistungsfähigkeit nicht in Anspruch nehmen. Unter Punkt 2 des Fragebogens in Anlage 1 muss angegeben werden, für welchen Teil des Auftrags diese Leistungsfähigkeit in Anspruch genommen wird. Duration of a supplier’s qualification A supplier's qualification is valid for a term of 5 years. After the 5-year period, the qualification may be extended for the same period after the administrative and/or technical files are updated. Infrabel Procurement sends the supplier an invitation in this regard about 6 months before the qualification's expiry date. The supplier shall submit the new administrative and/or technical file within 2 months. If the supplier does not take timely action, it runs the risk that its qualification extension is not completed before expiry date. Infrabel reserves the right to perform an audit, if this is deemed necessary, before extending the qualification. If these updated files and possible audit show that the supplier still meets the qualification conditions/criteria, the qualification of the supplier concerned will be renewed. The qualified supplier must continue to meet all qualification conditions/criteria throughout the qualification period. Įgaliotoji organizacija – pirkimams organizuoti, pirkimo procedūroms iki sutarties ar preliminariosios sutarties sudarymo atlikti, taip pat atlikto pirkimo procedūrų ataskaitai ar skelbimui apie sudarytą sutartį ar preliminariąją sutartį pateikti perkančiosios organizacijos įgaliota organizacija, nurodyta specialiosiose pirkimo sąlygose. Komisija – viešojo pirkimo komisija. Perkančioji organizacija – specialiosiose pirkimo sąlygose nurodyta perkančioji organizacija. Pirkimas – perkančiosios organizacijos atliekamas viešasis pirkimas. EBVPD pildomas jį įkėlus interneto svetainėje http://ebvpd.eviesiejipirkimai.lt/espd-web/. Tiekėjas, pildydamas EBVPD, laukelyje „Procedūros tipas“ turi pasirinkti „Atvira“. Section I: Program Overview & Background 1.1 Purpose The Department of the Air Force (DAF), Business and Enterprise Systems (BES) Directorate, AFLCMC/GBGD, is issuing this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) to identify and acquire an innovative, commercially available Digital Adoption Platform (DAP). User Productivity Kit (UPK), which is reaching its official end-of-life. The primary goal of this acquisition is to secure a modern, sustainable, enterprise-ready software-guided training and performance-support tool. It must streamline content creation, simplify software adoption, and provide real-time in-application guidance for the DEAMS user base. 1.2 Mission Impact & Capability Gap The current solution (Oracle UPK) represents unsupported software and significant technical debt. Its retirement creates a critical operational gap in how training is conducted across the enterprise. The replacement DAP will modernize training material outputs, provide interactive in-application assistance, and reduce the overall training footprint. This capability is designated as a Criticality (1) — Must Have requirement to support continuous financial and enterprise operations. 1.3 Scope of the Target Environment • User Base: Approximately 26,000+ geographically dispersed personnel across 170+ global locations. • Primary Integration: Stable and proven integration with Oracle e-Business Suite (EBS) (including F orms & OAF pages) and modern web applications. • Target Environments: The DAP must be deployable and tested across both Development (Dev) and Test environments before transitioning to

tate și confidențialitate a datelor gestionate, oferind protecție ridicată împotriva accesului neautorizat și a riscurilor cibernetice.  Creșterea transparenței și a trasabilității proceselor administrative la nivel local, astfel încât cetățenii să aibă o vizibilitate mai bună asupra activităților administrației publice.  Oferirea unei experiențe superioare de accesare a serviciilor publice, garantând conformitatea cu reglementările privind egalitatea de șanse, sustenabilitatea și durabilitatea, și adaptându-se nevoilor tuturor categoriilor de persoane.  Dezvoltarea competențelor digitale ale angajaților din administrația publică, ceea ce va duce la o mai bună înțelegere a conceptelor de administrație digitală și la eficientizarea proceselor de lucru. 2. CONTEXT ȘI NECESITATE 2.1. Analiza contextului și Cerințele utilizatorilor Proiectul "DigitalConnect Primăriile Avrămești, Săcel și Secuieni" se desfășoară în contextul necesității tot mai stringente de a accelera transformarea digitală în activitatea instituțiilor publice din administrația locală, în conformitate cu strategia regională aprobată pentru Regiunea Centru, care urmărește creșterea gradului de utilizare a serviciilor publice digitale. Acest proiect reprezintă un răspuns la dificultățile actuale în com

comunități din regiune, odată ce eficiența și beneficiile sale sunt demonstrate. Proiectul vizează atât cetățenii, cât și mediul de afaceri din cele trei unități administrativ- teritoriale – Primăriile Avrămești, Săcel și Secuieni – și are ca scop îmbunătățirea accesului acestora la serviciile publice digitale. Totodată, urmărește să schimbe în mod pozitiv percepția cetățenilor asupra administrației publice și să consolideze încrederea comunităților în calitatea și eficiența proceselor administrative locale. Având în vedere diferențele semnificative între cele trei parteneri din proiect — Primăriile Avrămești, Săcel și Secuieni — în ceea ce privește dotările hardware și software, fiecare beneficiind de o strategie investițională diferită și limitată, s-a considerat că abordarea optimă este testarea și pilotarea unor soluții SaaS de ultimă generație. Aceste soluții vor oferi partenerilor acces la infrastructură hardware și software modernă, îndeplinind cerințele stricte privind controlul costurilor, protecția mediului, accesibilitatea pentru toate categoriile sociale (inclusiv pentru persoanele cu dizabilități) și asigurarea disponibilității serviciilor publice digitale în regim non-stop (24/7). Astfel, proiectul va pune la dispoziția tuturor beneficiarilor – cetățeni,

pregătim instituțiile vizate pentru o tranziție completă către infrastructuri cloud și pentru alinierea la strategia națională privind cloud-ul guvernamental. La finalul proiectului, estimăm că numărul utilizatorilor, persoane fizice și juridice, care vor accesa constant soluțiile digitale implementate va depăși 10% din populația fiecăreia dintre cele trei comune, în ciuda diferențelor actuale de dotare și acces digital. Conform datelor de la ultimul recensământ, comuna Avrămești are aproximativ 2.100 de locuitori, comuna Săcel numără în jur de 1.500 de locuitori, iar comuna Secuieni are o populație de aproape 3.000 de locuitori. În ceea ce privește numărul de locuitori care efectuează plăți de taxe și impozite online, Primăria Avrămești are în prezent aproximativ 1.200 de utilizatori înregistrați în Sistemul Național Electronic de plată Ghiseul.ro, în timp ce Primăria Săcel figurează cu doar 75 de utilizatori, iar Primăria Secuieni cu 110 utilizatori. Totuși, numărul celor care utilizează alte servicii publice digitale (altele decât plățile de taxe și impozite) rămâne semnificativ mai mic în toate cele trei comune, situându-le sub pragul de 10% din populația actuală. Obiectivul proiectului este pilotarea și testarea serviciilor publice digitale, facilitând interconectarea și interoperabilitatea între instituțiile publice locale. Prin optimizarea interacțiunii dintre primăriile Avrămești, Săcel și Secuieni și mediul local, proiectul va accelera accesul cetățenilor la servicii digitale moderne, contribuind astfel la o administrație mai eficientă și la creșterea atractivității economice a regiunii. Soluțiile digitale prevăzute pentru dezvoltare în cadrul proiectului sunt scalabile și adaptabile, proiectate să gestioneze eficient un număr tot mai mare de utilizatori și volume de date aflate în continuă creștere. Aceste soluții sunt concepute să răspundă nevoilor atât ale mediului urban, cât și ale celui rural, asigurându-se că fiecare comunitate beneficiază de servicii moderne și flexibile, indiferent de dimensiunea și specificul său. Din perspectiva standardizării interacțiunii cu cetățenii și mediul de afaceri, soluțiile dezvoltate, testate și pilotate prin acest proiect vor aduce un nivel înalt de uniformitate în furnizarea serviciilor publice digitale. Această abordare va facilita semnificativ comunicarea și colaborarea între cetățeni, administrația locală și companii, încurajând adopția soluțiilor ele

valuării tehnice, și va acoperi un set de cerințe funcționale esențiale de natură legală și procedurală, ce trebuie îndeplinite încă de la depunerea ofertelor. One of the most concerning developments is the emergence of “nudify” or “nudifier” apps, which can turn ordinary photos or videos into sexualised material within seconds. In the past, altering photos, for example by people with a sexual interest in children, required skill and time. Today, premium options allow users of such apps to tailor audiovisual content to their preferences – including by age, ethnic background and other concerning criteria (ICMEC Australia, 2025). This represents a significant technological advance compared with a time when producing such material was far more complicated. The Australian online safety regulator (eSafety) took action against a UK-based company that offered three popular “nudify” services. According to eSafety, these services were used to create child sexual exploitation material, which constituted a breach of Australian online safety requirements. They may pretend to be younger than they really are, claim to be a different gender, give a false description of their appearance, or send photos of other people while pretending to be them ( catfishing). In some cases, a different scenario may unfold: it may be getting to know an adult who arouses the child’s curiosity and their desire to establish and maintain contact. Such a person is active in areas of the online world where children are present, for example, frequently using chats centred around young people’s interests. They may also search for children who match their individual preferences, for example by browsing their profiles on social media platforms or in online games. 14 The behaviours described here are often referred to by the term grooming. The term “grooming” more accurately reflects the gradual process by which an offender builds a relationship with a child, whereas “seduction” may refer to just one of the methods used https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/grooming [accessed: 30 March 2026]. 39 Some parents or carers are afraid of the internet. See also Terminology Guidelines for the Protection of Children from Sexual Exploitation and Sexual Abuse, https://ecpat.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/WYTYCZNE_ TERMINOLOGICZNE_ECPAT_FDDS_FINAL.pdf [accessed: 30 March 2026]. 46 The true scale of this phenomenon will never be fully known. This is due both to the constant emergence of new materials in this category and to the fact that content depicting the sexual abuse of children who are now adults continues to be distributed, despite the intensive efforts of many organisations involved in removing it from the virtual space. To give you some point of reference, however, we can cite estimates of how much content in the CSAM category is being uncovered. One of the main sources of information on this subject is the US CyberTipline mentioned earlier. Its data show, among other things, that a single image classified as CSAM was distributed for 19 years and appeared in more than 1.3 million reports! The statistical data published regularly are equally alarming. In 2024, almost 20 million reports were submitted to the helpline concerning the identification, in the resources of local Electronic Service Providers, of materials that may depict the sexual abuse of children (NCMEC, 2025). g such individuals, almost 70% of respondents said that they were constantly worried about being recognised by someone who had seen the materials depicting their sexual abuse. Meanwhile, 30% of respondents reported that they had been identified by such a person (CCCP, 2017). Numerous organisations around the world are involved in removing materials depicting the sexual abuse of children from virtual spaces. Despite the efforts being made, the problem remains current. The online world continues to be a place where content depicting the sexual abuse of children — regardless of their age or gender — is available, and statistics used as a reference point for estimating the scale of the phenomenon can be deeply distressing. That is why education about the risks associated with the internet that contribute to the creation of such materials is of key importance. Only through joint action and the involvement of different communities can the scale of this phenomenon be effectively reduced and the safety of the youngest users of the online world be ensured. 48 2.2.1 | When I create such content myself Among sexually charged audiovisual materials, there are also those considered to be self-generated17 by children. Older teenagers are probably more likely to admit to such experiences with greater ease and openness, while younger ones may find this difficult. This is precisely why younger children require greater attentiveness and sensitivity from adults. Although sexting as part of exploring one’s own sexuality among peers can sometimes lead to positive experiences, it is important to be aware of the risks associated with it. These include, among other things, the distribution of intimate material after a relationship has ended, for example, as an act of revenge by one of the parties. Particular caution is needed when an adult is involved in sexting. Depending on the circumstances, such behaviour may even constitute a criminal offence. 2.1.2 | Grooming and manipulation The second group of behaviours we want to tell you about are those associated with grooming 14 online. Be aware that a person who wants to sexually harm your child may use various methods and techniques to get closer to them and gain their trust. They may pretend to be younger than they really are, claim to be a different gender, give a false description of their appearance, or send photos of other people while pretending to be them ( catfishing). creating CSAM, this often concerns children in her care, including her own children. She usually does so together with a partner or another man (Bickart et al., 2019; Salter et al., 2021). Women may also act alone – in such cases, creating such content may be linked to relationships with other people, including men, and involvement in wider networks of perpetrators (Salter et al., 2021). This shows that we cannot assume that women are “less dangerous” – it is important to remain vigilant towards all adults who have contact with our children, regardless of gender. When it is not clear who this adult is to the child, then significant precautions really must be taken. We need to try not so much to monitor, but also to ask about more general aspects of the relationship, because this can help us determine where it is heading. At the same time, research findings show that early exposure to such content is relatively common and that it may be accidental or unintentional (Dieseth et al., 2026). In the case of adult online behaviour involving drawing children into sexual activity (e.g. asking for photos or engaging in sexually explicit conversations), research indicates that perpetrators are often people known to the child, and many such situations are an extension of existing social relationships (Finkelhor, Turner and Colburn, 2022). Similar findings emerge from research concerning children who were sexually abused directly (offline), with audiovisual materials from these situations subsequently being uploaded to the internet. In such cases, the perpetrators were most often parents, people known to the child or their family, or people in positions of trust (CCCP, 2017). This is consistent with findings indicating that a significant proportion of CSAM is created in the home environment (Salter et al., 2023). Grooming a child online is a way of involving them in sexual activity for which they are not developmentally ready, which they are unable to fully understand or give informed consent to. This may involve sexual conversations as well as the sending of intimate material. The person behind this behaviour may also want to meet the child in the real world. The less information they have about the child, the better; it will be more difficult for them to arouse their interest and gain their trust. 41 2.1.3 | Sexual extortion The behaviour described here was the focus of a campaign called “SayNO!”, launched by the European Cybercrime Centre in 2017 (EC3, 2017), which was also supported by the Polish police (Policja, 2017). The campaign was prompted by tragic events involving children, including cases of self-harm, suicide attempts and suicides. Despite the passage of several years and the considerable efforts of the international community, sexual extortion continues to occur online, and its scale and reach are also increasing. 42 A child will not come to confide in us that they are feeling bad, that they have some problems, because they may decide that either we will not help them with these problems, or that we do not have time, or cannot help them because

In 2024, NCMEC received almost 100 reports a day concerning financially motivated sexual extortion. Since 2021, at least 36 suicides among teenage boys have been linked to this phenomenon. There has also been an increase in reports of violence against children perpetrated by various online groups. These activities involve encouraging minors to self-harm, harm other people and engage in sexual behaviour, including with peers or their own siblings (NCMEC, 2025). In 2024, the CyberTipline15, operated by NCMEC, received more than 1,300 reports related to this activity, an increase of more than 200% compared with the previous year. award_criteria.text: 1.1 The Office of the Revenue Commissioners (“Revenue Commissioners”) invites tenders (“Tenders”) to this request for tenders (“RFT”) from economic operators (“Tenderers”) for the provision of the goods and services as described in Appendix 1 to this RFT (the “Goods and“Services”). 1.2 In summary, the Goods and Services comprise: Provision of ICT Training via an Online Training Platform. 1.3 The Revenue Commissioners (Revenue) is seeking a provider of an e-learning platform to support the continuing professional development of staff in its ICT function. Revenue requires a platform for 200 users that provides access to relevant, high-quality learning content on current technologies and industry practices. The platform should have a clear, intuitive catalogue that enables users to easily search for and access relevant learning materials. The provider must ensure that content is regularly reviewed and updated to reflect developments in technology and industry practices. The successful provider will also be expected to provide a responsive customer success team that works collaboratively with Revenue to support the effective use of the platform and adapt to Revenue’s evolving learning needs throughout the contract term. 1.4 This public procurement competition (the “Competition”) will be conducted in accordance with the open procedure under the European Union (Award of Public Authority Contracts) Regulations 2016 (Statutory Instrument 284 of 2016) (the “Regulations”). 1.5 Any contract that may result from this Competition (the “Goods and Services Contract”) will be issued for a term of 3 years (“the Term”). The current legacy analog infrastructure limits scalability, resilience, and interoperability. Under this Call for Solutions, the selected vendor will deliver, integrate, install, and acceptance-test a flexible, open-standard, modular Digital IF solution across up to twenty (20) worldwide satellite communications (SATCOM) teleport sites. Increment 1 will establish a fully operational baseline designed to support subsequent capability upgrades and integrations in future fiscal years. However, before committing to a full-scale global deployment, the DoW must validate the operation, interoperability, security, and performance of these modular commercial solutions in a rigorous representative environment. Technical Objective & Scope The DoW seeks a commercial solution for an Increment 1 Digital IF capability set built on a flexible, open standard (e.g., Digital Intermediate Frequency Interoperability compliant), modular architecture. The selected solution will undergo standard site acceptance testing and operational verification to confirm compliance with contract performance requirements and site compatibility. Upon successful acceptance, this operational configuration will serve as the standardized baseline for deployment and installation across up to twenty (20) worldwide SATCOM teleport sites. Mission Impact Successful validation and deployment of this flexible open-standard Digital IF architecture will directly enhance warfighter lethality and survivability by delivering a highly resilient, agile, and survivable GEO-SATCOM capability which rapidly adapts to contested/congested environments. The current legacy analog infrastructure limits scalability, resilience, and interoperability. Under this Call for Solutions, the selected vendor will deliver, integrate, install, and acceptance-test a flexible, open-standard, modular Digital IF solution across up to twenty (20) worldwide satellite communications (SATCOM) teleport sites. Increment 1 will establish a fully operational baseline designed to support subsequent capability upgrades and integrations in future fiscal years. SECTION 2 – REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION PROBLEM STATEMENT Area of Interest: Modular Digital Intermediate Frequency Solu

quires an open-standard Digital IF architecture. However, before committing to a full-scale global deployment, the DoW must validate the operation, interoperability, security, and performance of these modular commercial solutions in a rigorous representative environment. Technical Objective & Scope The DoW seeks a commercial solution for an Increment 1 Digital IF capability set built on a flexible, open standard (e.g., Digital Intermediate Frequency Interoperability compliant), modular architecture. The selected solution will undergo standard site acceptance testing and operational verification to confirm compliance with contract performance requirements and site compatibility. Upon successful acceptance, this operational configuration will serve as the standardized baseline for deployment and installation across up to twenty (20) worldwide SATCOM teleport sites. Mission Impact Successful validation and deployment of this flexible open-standard Digital IF architecture will directly enhance warfighter lethality and survivability by delivering a highly resilient, agile, and survivable GEO-SATCOM capability which rapidly adapts to contested/congested environments. BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) Office of Infrastructure Research & Development (HRDI) conducts and oversees research and development programs and projects that address critical highway infrastructure needs and priorities of national importance. Research studies focus on the design, materials, construction, operation, and preservation of highway pavements, bridges, and other structure

rs, engineers, and transportation agencies nationwide through the FHWA InfoHighway™ data portals (https://infohighway.fhwa.dot.gov). FHWA InfoHighway provides centralized access to research-quality infrastructure performance data, supporting data-driven pavement engineering, predictive modeling, and State DOT decision-making. The primary mission of the LPES contract is direct support for the LTPP program, consolidating field data collection, pavement research analytics, and long-term data management; additionally, the contract provides direct and indirect data support to related FHWA infrastructure research programs. 2 OBJECTIVE/SCOPE OF WORK The main objective of this contract is to provide highly specialized engineering services, including field survey operations, data quality management, scientific data curation, and technology transfer support services for the LTPP program and related highway infrastructure research initiatives. earch- grade data quality. • Formulate strategic pavement research plans advancing the LTPP program, conduct targeted performance case studies, and deliver practical engineering tools, Section 508- compliant publications, and technical webinars. • Develop and curate specialized, analysis-ready datasets for machine learning (ML) and predictive modeling across LTPP and broader highway infrastructure domains, integrating modern database architectures and coordinating data schemas with web portal contractors for public release. To fulfill the LTPP program mission and support broader FHWA pavement and other infrastructure research, the scope of work is organized across three (3) primary Task Areas. For the purpose of evaluation only, bidders are requested to propose an annual PR plan based on an indicative out-of-pocket budget of €50,000 excluding VAT per annum. This indicative budget is provided solely to allow for a comparable assessment of proposals. Actual annual implementation budgets, scope and allocation will be subject to approval by the Contracting Authority and may vary during the contract period. For the sake of this exercise, bidders will be assessed for the PR ideas they pitch in the proposed plan for the destination with an out-of-pocket budget of €50,000 excluding VAT. Expenses related to press and influencer hosting in Malta for press and influence trips (travel costs, accommodation, transport and ground handling) should not be factored into this budget, as these are absorbed by a separate and independent budget at MTA head office. A plan proposal for 1 year should be provided, with ideas ranging from special one- off PR projects and promotions in France as well as cross-branding PR & influence opportunities. The ideas proposed must be realistic and feasible, with the possibility to be implemented at the budget cost estimate proposed. The objective of such a plan is to generate and cultivate the best positive exposure in B2B and B2C commu

posure for the Maltese Islands. 5. The current legacy analog infrastructure limits scalability, resilience, and interoperability. Under this Call for Solutions, the selected vendor will deliver, integrate, install, and acceptance-test a flexible, open-standard, modular Digital IF solution across up to twenty (20) worldwide satellite communications (SATCOM) teleport sites. Increment 1 will establish a fully operational baseline designed to support subsequent capability upgrades and integrations in future fiscal years. SECTION 2 – REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION PROBLEM STATEMENT Area of Interest: Modular Digital Intermediate Frequency Solu

quires an open-standard Digital IF architecture. However, before committing to a full-scale global deployment, the DoW must validate the operation, interoperability, security, and performance of these modular commercial solutions in a rigorous representative environment. Technical Objective & Scope The DoW seeks a commercial solution for an Increment 1 Digital IF capability set built on a flexible, open standard (e.g., Digital Intermediate Frequency Interoperability compliant), modular architecture. The selected solution will undergo standard site acceptance testing and operational verification to confirm compliance with contract performance requirements and site compatibility. Upon successful acceptance, this operational configuration will serve as the standardized baseline for deployment and installation across up to twenty (20) worldwide SATCOM teleport sites. Mission Impact Successful validation and deployment of this flexible open-standard Digital IF architecture will directly enhance warfighter lethality and survivability by delivering a highly resilient, agile, and survivable GEO-SATCOM capability which rapidly adapts to contested/congested environments. The current legacy analog infrastructure limits scalability, resilience, and interoperability. Under this Call for Solutions, the selected vendor will deliver, integrate, install, and acceptance-test a flexible, open-standard, modular Digital IF solution across up to twenty (20) worldwide satellite communications (SATCOM) teleport sites. Increment 1 will establish a fully operational baseline designed to support subsequent capability upgrades and integrations in future fiscal years. SECTION 2 – REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION PROBLEM STATEMENT Area of Interest: Modular Digital Intermediate Frequency Solu

quires an open-standard Digital IF architecture. However, before committing to a full-scale global deployment, the DoW must validate the operation, interoperability, security, and performance of these modular commercial solutions in a rigorous representative environment. Technical Objective & Scope The DoW seeks a commercial solution for an Increment 1 Digital IF capability set built on a flexible, open standard (e.g., Digital Intermediate Frequency Interoperability compliant), modular architecture. The selected solution will undergo standard site acceptance testing and operational verification to confirm compliance with contract performance requirements and site compatibility. Upon successful acceptance, this operational configuration will serve as the standardized baseline for deployment and installation across up to twenty (20) worldwide SATCOM teleport sites. Mission Impact Successful validation and deployment of this flexible open-standard Digital IF architecture will directly enhance warfighter lethality and survivability by delivering a highly resilient, agile, and survivable GEO-SATCOM capability which rapidly adapts to contested/congested environments. The Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Technical Assistance Facility under the Learning Acceleration in Secondary Education (LAISE) Program and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include undertaking a comprehensive assessment of ICT infrastructure and institutional readiness, the status and readiness of Multimedia Classrooms (MMCs), and teachers’ competencies and readiness to deliver ICT-enabled teaching using ICT facilities and MMCs.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: www.dshe.gov.bd or can be obtained at the address given below. The duration of the assignment will be about 06 (Six) months. The assignment is expected to commence in March 2027.

The Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education now invites eligible firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Expressions of Interest will be assessed based on the follo

igible firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Expressions of Interest will be assessed based on the following criteria:

  • General Experience of the Firm (core business and years in business).
  • Experience in similar assignments of compatible size, complexity and technical specialty in the required area. Experience in development partner-financed contracts will be considered an advantage.
  • Firm’s in-house staffing resources with relevant expertise (extent of relevant expertise available among the staff who are on the firm’s regular payroll). 
  • Firm’s relevant organizational capabilities for the assignment.

Key Experts will not be evaluated during the assessment of Expressions of Interest.

Consultants are requested to submit but not limited to, the following supporting documents in support of the above-mentioned criteria:

(a) The Firm's Incorporation/Trade/Registration documents from the country of the firm; (b) JV agreement/letter of intent (if applicable); (c) Firm’s brochure;

D1-508 „Dėl Aplinkos apsaugos kriterijų taikymo, vykdant žaliuosius pirkimus, tvarkos aprašo patvirtinimo“ 4.1 punkte, 4.3 punkte arba 4.4 punkto 4.4.4.1 papunktyje: Prekių tiekimo metu turi būti siekiama mažinti popieriaus sunaudojimą ir atsisakoma nebūtino dokumentų kopijavimo ir spausdinimo. Jei tiekėjas vykdydamas sutartį taps PVM mokėtoju, jis pasiūlyme turi nurodyti kainą su PVM. Pasiūlymų kainos bus vertinamos ir lyginamos su visais mokesčiais, įskaitant PVM. Tuo atveju, kai mokesčius reguliuojančių įstatymų ir jų įgyvendinamųjų teisės aktų nustatyta tvarka pirkimo vykdytojas pats turi sumokėti PVM į valstybės biudžetą už įsigytą pirkimo objektą, šis mokestis įskaičiuojamas į pasiūlymo kainą (jeigu tiekėjas jo neįskaičiavo pateikdamas pasiūlymą, palyginimo tikslais jį įskaičiuoja pats pirkimo vykdytojas). Į pasiūlymo kainą privalo būti įskaičiuoti visi mokesčiai bei visos kitos tiekėjo patirtos ir (ar) galimos patirti tiesioginės ir netiesioginės išlaidos ir mokesčiai, susiję su pirkimo objektu (išskyrus tuos atvejus, kai konkretaus pirkimo sąlygose aiškiai nurodyta, kad tam tikros konkrečios išlaidos neturi būti įskaičiuotos į sutarties kainą. 4.6. Bendra pasiūlymo kaina (sąnaudos) su PVM turi būti nurodyta dviejų skaitmenų po kablelio tikslumu. Šią kainą sudarančios kainos sudedamosios dalys ar įkainiai turi būti nurodyta dviejų skaitmenų po kablelio tikslumu. 4.7. Tiekėjas gali užšifruoti teikiam

Tiekėjas, nusprendęs pateikti užšifruotą pasiūlymą, turi: 4.7.1.1. iki konkrečių pasiūlymų pateikimo termino pabaigos naudodamasis CVP IS priemonėmis pateikti užšifruotą pasiūlymą (užšifruojamas visas pasiūlymas arba pasiūlymo dokumentas, kuriame nurodyta pasiūlymo kaina). Instrukcija, kaip tiekėjui užšifruoti pasiūlymą galima rasti Viešųjų pirkimų tarnybos interneto svetainėje. 4.7.1.2. iki pirminio susipažinimo su pasiūlymais vokų atplėšimo procedūros („vokų atplėšimo“) pradžios (kaip nustatyta šio konkretaus pirkimo sąlygų 4.1 punkte) CVP IS susirašinėjimo priemonėmis pateikti slaptažodį, su kuriuo pirkimo vykdytojas galės iššifruoti pateiktą pasiūlymą. Iškilus CVP IS techninėms problemoms, kai tiekėjas neturi galimybės pateikti slaptažodžio per CVP IS susirašinėjimo priemonę, tiekėjas turi teisę slaptažodį pateikti kitomis priemonėmis pasirinktinai: pirkimo vykdytojo oficialiu elektroniniu paštu, faksu arba raštu. Tokiu atveju tiekėjas turėtų būti aktyvus ir įsitikinti, kad pateiktas slaptažodis laiku pasiekė adresatą (pavyzdžiui, susisiekęs su pirkimo vykdytoju oficialiu jo telefonu ir (arba) kitais būdais). 4.7.2. The purpose of this procedure is to establish a Panel of Trainers for the provision of Training Services for the Local Enterprise Office in Leitrim County Council. LEO Leitrim is compiling a panel of trainers, from which future training programmes, workshops and seminars for a maximum of a 3 year period will be selected . Applications are invited from those with appropriate skills and experience that wish to be included in the LEO Leitrim Training panel. For the purposes of this document, the term “Trainer” refers to any Applicant admitted to the Panel and engaged by Local Enterprise Office Leitrim to deliver training services. References to Tenderer, Consultant or Applicant shall be interpreted accordingly. The proposed Training Services include but are not limited to those set out in section below. The Leitrim Local Enterprise Office serves as a first stop shop to provide support and services to start, grow and develop micro and small businesses in County Leitrim. LEO Leitrim Training Services are aimed at improving owner-manager skills to assist the survival and growth of micro- businesses. As per the Enterprise Development Plan, the provision of training is a fundamental aspect of LEO supports to entrepreneurs in the county. The Local Enterprise Office cur

Therefore, the service is not fully subject to the provisions of Directive 2014/24/EU. Given the strategic partnership of this service, the Contracting Authority considers the creation of a Panel as the most appropriate and workable procurement process for the provision of eBooks. A Panel constitutes a means of assessing the financial and technical capacity of a number of economic operators to whom individual contracts may or may not be awarded over the Panel’s duration. The Contracting Authority is planning to run a two-stage tender process. In the initial stage, all providers who meet the Selection Criteria included in the Qualification Questionnaire Document will be admitted to the Panel. The second stage of this competition is Contracts. Contracts will be signed by the Contracting Authority with each provider, identifying the terms and conditions including the scope of the services, costs and any other operations terms required. The DPS will provide an ongoing mechanism that allows suitably qualified suppliers who meet the minimum eligibility and quality thresholds to apply for admission at any time during the life of the system. Unlike a traditional framework agreement, the DPS is fully electronic and remains open throughout its duration. Once admitted to the DPS, suppliers may be invited to participate in mini competitions for specific training requirements as they arise. Contracts will be awarded following these mini competitions in accordance with the applicable procurement rules. The DPS will operate in line with the provisions of the relevant procurement directives and will remain in place for a period of three years. Suppliers may join or leave the DPS at any stage du

Medium enterprises: enterprises which are neither micro nor small, which employ fewer than 250 persons and which have an annual turnover not exceeding Euro 50 million, and/or an annual balance sheet total not exceeding Euro 43 million. certifications_partner.text: z Wojciechem Manajem, Dyrektorem Centralnego Laboratorium Dozoru Technicznego. Laboratoria mobilne są częścią tworzonej przez UDT sie- ci badawczej. Urząd oferuje wsparcie diagnostyczne w ramach swojej działalności, tym samym zapewniając bezpieczną eksploatację urzą- dzeń technicznych. Obecne zagrożenie epidemiologiczne rewiduje gotowość poszczegól- nych przedsiębiorstw do utrzymania ciągłości działania. Standard ISO 22301 ma więcej elementów i wymagań niż te, które wiążą się z podjęty- mi przez organizację działaniami w wyniku trwającej pandemii. Z kolej- nego artykułu dowiedzą się Państwo, jakie korzyści płyną z wdrożenia wymagań nowej ISO 22301. Zapraszamy do części pierwszej cyklu artykułów poświęconych za- gadnieniom bezpiecznej eksploatacji urządzeń transportu bliskie- go. Posługując się pojęciem resursu, ekspert UDT odpowiada na pytania, czy projektowany okres eksploatacji tych urządzeń nie został już przekroczony. W kolejnym artykule dotyczącym urządzeń ziębniczych autor przybli- ża pojawiający się coraz częściej szczególny przypadek wprowadzanej zmiany, związany z chęcią zwiększenia bezpieczeństwa amoniakalnej instalacji ziębniczej poprzez ograniczenie potencjalnych konsekwencji uwolnienia tego czynnika. Doświadczenia i obserwacje dotyczące różnic pomiędzy realizacją bez

ny, związany z chęcią zwiększenia bezpieczeństwa amoniakalnej instalacji ziębniczej poprzez ograniczenie potencjalnych konsekwencji uwolnienia tego czynnika. Doświadczenia i obserwacje dotyczące różnic pomiędzy realizacją bez- pośrednią analiz HAZOP a realizacją tych analiz w wersji on-line przed- stawia ekspert UDT w kolejnym materiale. Na tle wypracowanych doświadczeń w realizacji analiz bezpośrednich opisuje możliwości pro- wadzenia analiz zdalnie. W dalszej części numeru prezentujemy relację z wręczenia certyfikatów UDT-CERT, pierwszej w Polsce jednostki certyfikującej systemy, która otrzy- mała akredytację PCA w zakresie normy PN-EN ISO 50001. UDT-CERT oce- niła i potwierdziła pełne wdrożenie oraz stosowanie Systemu Zarządzania Energią w KGHM Polska Miedź S.A. oraz „Energetyka” sp. z o.o. Polecam również artykuł dotyczący dostępności cyfrowej, informacyjnej, komunikacyjnej i architektonicznej w UDT. W trudnym czasie pandemii warto pamiętać, że osoby ze szczególnymi potrzebami są obecne w na- szym otoczeniu, a wpływ na dostępność ma każdy z nas. Kolejny rok minął pod znakiem zmian w przepisach prawa dotyczą- cych funkcjonowania UDT. W artykule opisane są inicjatywy legislacyj- ne ukierunkowane z jednej strony na umożliwienie zachowania ciągłości działania przedsiębiorstw i ins

However, the deployment of nuclear technologies is not limited to technological advancement; it also requires full compliance with rigorous safety and quality standards that underpin trust in the nuclear energy sector. Modern nuclear facilities, due to their technical complexity, extended lifecy- cle, and critical importance to public safety and environmental protection, require a rigorous approach to quality management at every stage — from design and construction through to operation and eventual decommission- ing. For this reason, clearly defined and effectively implemented quality assurance (QA) systems are essential. QA systems are a core element of nuclear project management, ensuring not only high standards of execu- tion, but above all, the safe operation of nuclear facilities throughout their entire lifecycle. The manufacturing of elements for the nuclear energy sector is subject to exceptionally stringent requirements concerning quality, safety, and regulatory oversight. Given the potential consequences of equipment failure in environments involving ionizing radiation and high-pressure conditions, every element of nuclear infrastructure must comply with strict technical and legal stan- dards. Is it permissible for the company responsible for the design to obtain an EU-Type examination – design type certificate and the fabricator obtain an appropriate certifica- te for the manufacturing phase, e.g. Modules F (Conformity to type based on pressure equipment verification)? Anserw No. Even if different organisations can be involved, the directive clearly indica- tes that there can be only one manufacturer who is responsible for design, manufacture and conformity assessment of the pressure equipment. The manufacturer may subcontract tasks in relation to design and/or ma- nufacture but must retain overall control and have the necessary compe- tence to take the responsibility for the product. AP-1000 The nuclear power project currently the closest to construction stage in Poland is being developed by the consortium of Westinghouse Electric Company (WEC) and BECHTEL. The consortium is proposing the AP1000 pressurised water reactor (PWR), with an electrical output exceeding 1100 MWe (3400 MWt). This reactor design is already in commercial operation in both the United States and China. A distinguishing feature of the AP1000 are its passive safety systems, including the Passive Core Cooling System and the Passive Containment Cooling System, which rely on natural convection and gravity, rather than electrically powered pumps. STATEMENT OF WORK C. 1. OVERVIEW/BACKGROUND. The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory

The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. The Contractor shall report all contract sales under this contract as follows: (1) The Contractor shall accurately report the dollar value, in U.S. dollars and rounded to the nearest whole dollar, of all sales under this contract by calendar quarter (January 1-March 31, April 1-June 30, July 1-September 30, and October 1-December 31). The dollar value of a sale is the price paid by the Schedule user for products and services on a Schedule task or delivery order. The reported contract sales value shall include the Industrial Funding Fee (IFF). The Contractor shall maintain a consistent accounting method of sales reporting, based on the Contractor's established commercial accounting practice. The acceptable points at which sales may be reported include– (i) Receipt of order; (ii) Shipment or delivery, as applicable; (iii) Issuance of an invoice; or (iv) Payment. (2) Contract sales shall be reported to FSS within 30 calendar days following the completion of each reporting quarter. The Contractor shall continue to furnish quarterly reports, including “zero” sales, through physical completion of the last outstanding task order or delivery order of the contract. (3) Reportable sales under the contract are those resulting from sales of contract items to authorized users unless the purchase was conducted pursuant to a separate contracting authority such as a Governmentwide Acquisition Contract (GWAC); a separately awarded FAR Part 12, FAR Part 13, FAR Part 14, or FAR Part 15 procurement; or a non-FAR contract. To meet these ESR bunch injection schemes and requirements, an array of stripline-based kickers, individually fed by high voltage (HV) pulse signals of up to +/-30 kV, will be installed in the ESR. The required deflection angle is in the range 1- 1.5 mrad, for the individual stripline kicker we target a deflection angle of ~125 µrad @ 18 GeV, assuming +/-27 kV pulse supply voltage between the kicker electrodes. To keep the losses of the stored beam low, a ~15 σ distance between the stored beam and the injection septa in the ESR must be maintained, which translates into a minimum physical aperture of 30 mm diameter for the stripline kickers. To meet these ESR bunch injection schemes and requirements, an array of stripline-based kickers, individually fed by high voltage (HV) pulse signals of up to +/-30 kV, will be installed in the ESR. The required deflection angle is in the range 1- 1.5 mrad, for the individual stripline kicker we target a deflection angle of ~125 µrad @ 18 GeV, assuming +/-27 kV pulse supply voltage between the kicker electrodes. To keep the losses of the stored beam low, a ~15 σ distance between the stored beam and the injection septa in the ESR must be maintained, which translates into a minimum physical aperture of 30 mm diameter for the stripline kickers. Ces documents, signés par le déposant, indiquent au profit de qui le cautionnement est constitué, son affectation précise par l'indication des références du contrat et de son objet ainsi que le nom, les prénoms et l'adresse complète du contractant et éventuellement, du tiers qui a effectué le dépôt pour compte, avec la mention " bailleur de fonds " ou " mandataire " suivant le cas. Dans les cas où le cautionnement est constitué par un tiers, celui-ci est caution solidaire. La preuve de constitution doit être transmise à l’attention du pouvoir adjudicateur En cas de manquement dans le cadre de l’exécution du présent contrat, même lorsqu’il y a résolution ou résiliation du contrat, la Ville prélève d’office sur le cautionnement les sommes qui lui reviennent. Lorsque le montant du cautionnement n’atteint plus le montant indiqué ci-avant par suite d’un prélèvement d’office opéré par la Ville, le cautionnement doit être reconstitué dans les trente jours du prélèvement. DESCRIPTION Travaux publics et Services gouvernementaux Canada (TPSGC), au nom de Recherche et Développement pour la Défense Canada, Centre de recherche de Valcartier publie cette demande d’offres pour l’achat de services en recherche et développement lié au domaine du C4ISR (Commandement, contrôle, communications, informatique, renseignement, surveillance et reconnaissance). Le besoin vise la recherche et le développement de capacités C4ISR de nouvelle génération afin d'améliorer la connaissance de la situation et la prise de décision dans des opérations militaires multi-domaines (terre, air, mer, espace, cyber et information). Les travaux porteront sur l'intégration et l'exploitation de données provenant de sources variées en utilisant l'intelligence artificielle, l'apprentissage automatique et la fusion de données multimodales. L'objectif est de concevoir des systèmes agiles, adaptatifs et reconfigurables capables de s'ajuster rapidement à l'évolution des missions et des menaces, tout en maintenant la supervision humaine. Les activités comprendront la conception de cadres conceptuels C4ISR, le développement d'outils d'intégration, d'analyse et de visualisation des données, la recherche sur la fusion de capteurs basée sur l'IA, l'adaptation des c
